title: Charles V to his ambassadors in England (Simon Renard, "lieutenant d'Amont"), Brussels, 24 January 1554: the cipher passage on Besançon BM Ms 1582, f. 2, with its contemporary decipherment

steps.what: Scans of Ms 1580 f. 239 and Ms 1582 f. 2 requested from the Bibliothèque municipale de Besançon; received free for research on 18 Nov 2026.
Two blind transcriptions with the margin masked; reconciled sign by sign (transcription/).

Key re-derived by aligning the cipher with the contemporary decipherment on the page; rule base letter + vowel mark fitted; split-page hold-out 0.726 / 0.691 against shuffled keys at most 0.25 (seed alignment used both pages).

Weiss IV no. LXIII (lacuna at this passage), Gachard IV app. CLV (full minute), CSP Spain XII pp. 44-49, Pich-Ponce 2024 (the cipher, published), Cryptiana March 2026: the text and the key are in print.

Decoded cipher compared with the contemporary decipherment and with the printed minute: the minute agrees with the cipher against the decipherment in 21 places, with the decipherment in 1 (divergences_vs_minute.tsv); key structure matches Pich-Ponce 2024.
358 words: 210 sure, 125 probable, 4 restored, 19 in two lines not transcribed (reading.md).

Lines r24 and v26, cut off in the first crops, transcribed from the full scans in two new blind passes and arbitrated (46 signs, 42 in full agreement, 1 differing by a mark, 3 differing; transcription/cut_lines_r24_v26.tsv).

Re-derived key compared with Pich-Ponce 2024 (her text and printed tables; not reproduced): the 8 plain-digit entries (8, 7, 9, 6, 4, 2, 3 written z, 66; 185 occurrences) give her values; 10 two-figure entries (rr, u, w, r6, r8, ry, rs, r3, n, nz; 252 occurrences) give her values if their hooked first stroke is read 1 or 2 as her series requires (not checked shape by shape), w and nz each being two of her numerals (20 a / 10 l; 17 d / 12 i); 48 of 60 syllable entries (375 of 416 occurrences) follow her stated rule (preceding letter plus vowel mark), and for 3 of the other 12 (c: do, 6_ ci, mt na) her rule fits the minute where our alignment did not; m'. (our n) is her 'no'. Values not transferred into key.tsv or the reading.
358 words: 215 sure, 131 probable, 12 restored (reading.md); r24 and v26 read from the cipher.

Write-up check (AI agent for the maintainers): the local DECODE record list (10,106 records, harvested to 30 Oct 2026) searched for Besançon, Granvelle and Renard: no record of Ms 1582 f. 2 (the one hit, R9959, is Renard to Prince Philip, 19 Feb 1554, at Simancas, another letter); catalogue.json and research/leads.json hold no entry for this leaf. Words of reading.md recounted: 357 if the word split over v3-v4 is one word, 214 sure if the half-word that opens the leaf ([no]stre) is counted as restored; the contributor's count is 215 of 358. One word apart, same class.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1120 tokens, 139 types, fr-1530-despatches order 4: reading -2.461 per letter; random keys -4.07 (z 6.8); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.475 (mean -2.534, z 2.4); annealer on the real text -2.357. Verdict: underdetermined.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.461; polyphony 0.0; 1 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.357

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Decode of the cipher with a key re-derived here from the leaf's own contemporary decipherment (EM alignment of the blind transcription with the decipherment written around the cipher), checked against the minute printed by Gachard (1882); the key's structure matches the cipher published by Pich-Ponce (2024), found afterwards.

The whole text is in print (Gachard 1882), hence class already solved; the extent of what was decoded here is partial.

outcome.notes: No image of the Bibliothèque municipale de Besançon is reproduced. The library dates the leaf 1555; the text is the letter of 24 Jan 1554.

texts.label: Ms 1582, f. 2r-v: Charles V to his ambassadors in England, 24 Jan 1554 (cipher passage)
texts.summary: Charles V tells his ambassadors in London how to answer the French peace overtures: he has always wanted peace, the French broke the truce of their own will, his proposal of September 1553 made at the request of the Cardinal of Imola (Dandino) was never answered; he will negotiate through Mary Tudor once French terms for peace or truce are known; Renard is to learn from Paget what the French ambassador said about marriage matches.

reading_review.by: integration review of PR #788 (AI agent, for the maintainers); not a person
reading_review.note: Grade given by the reviewer, not by the author of the reading: stated in the review of pull request #788 and entered here at the reviewer's request. reading.md read as sentences against translation.md: coherent French (Charles V to his ambassadors in England, 24 Jan 1554: the French peace overtures, the proposal of September 1553, Mary Tudor as go-between, Paget and the marriage matches); about a third of the words are probable for key-side reasons stated in reading.md (nus/pur for nous/pour, w a/l, mt/nt), so the text is raw rather than clean. A decoder written by the reviewer from key.tsv reproduces 48 of the 50 lines of decryption.tsv exactly (the two others differ only on a sign with no key value); r24 and v26 decoded by the reviewer from cut_lines_r24_v26.tsv give the stated readings. The gloss and the cipher were compared with Gachard's minute in print. Transcription not checked against images (the library's images are not public). A model's reading: no person has checked it.
